newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Strike closes down Israeli banks.
newsitem.headline: Strike closes down Israeli banks.

text.p: Most banks in Israel closed on Friday due to a strike by bank workers, in violation of a court ruling the workers could strike for only half the day, a senior banker said.
It was the second consecutive Friday that the workers refused to work, demanding a five-day work week. Banks in Israel are currently operate from Sunday through Friday.
Banks at border crossings and direct banking services remained open on Friday, as well as some of the smaller banks.

"The labour court ruled the workers and management had to get into intense negotiations to reach a settlement," said Bank Association director Freddy Vider. "It also decided there wouldn't be a complete strike today or any other day."
But Bank Leumi Workers Committee head Louis Roth said the decision to allow a strike for half a day was unreasonable.

"Does the court want us to throw out customers in the middle of the day? The result would be much worse," he told Israel Radio. He added customers could use automatic tellers for many services on Friday.
Israel's Consumer Council warned the bank workers' behaviour signalled a dangerous use of "strong-arm tactics" that could threaten other areas of the economy.
Vider, asked by the radio whether the banks would sue the workers unions, said: "Each bank separately will decide. I think it is necessary to carry out the law in Israel."
